question: A 26-year-old woman comes to the emergency department 30 minutes after she was bitten by her neighbor's cat. She has no history of serious illness and takes no medications. She received all recommended immunizations during childhood but has not received any since then. Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows four puncture wounds on the thenar eminence of the right hand. There is mild swelling but no erythema. There is normal range of motion of her right thumb and wrist. The wound is cleaned with povidone iodine and irrigated with saline. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

options.opd: Close the wound with cyanoacrylate tissue adhesive
options.ope: Administer tetanus toxoid and tetanus IV immunoglobulin

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Cat bite -> potential introduction of bacteria into the wound -> risk of infection -> 80% CHAIN: Puncture wounds on the hand -> increased risk of tetanus infection -> 70% CHAIN: Tetanus infection risk -> administration of tetanus toxoid and tetanus IV immunoglobulin recommended -> 80%
enhanced_information: Given the risk of tetanus infection from puncture wounds on the hand, the most appropriate next step in management is to administer tetanus toxoid and tetanus IV immunoglobulin to prevent tetanus infection.
analysis: Given the risk of tetanus infection from puncture wounds on the hand, the most appropriate next step in management is to administer tetanus toxoid and tetanus IV immunoglobulin to prevent tetanus infection. This aligns with standard medical practice guidelines for wound management in this scenario.
